items.case: A service account should read one reporting folder but no others.
items.answer: Define approved identity, positive allowed read and negative forbidden read, expected result, evidence and rollback.
items.evidence: Scope record and paired test outcomes.
items.pitfall: One successful read doesn't establish least privilege.

items.case: A moderate weakness disrupts payroll during a deadline.
items.answer: Compare exposure, exploit prerequisites, timing, financial impact and controls with assumptions disclosed.
items.evidence: Business consequence, decision rubric and residual risk.
items.pitfall: Technical severity alone doesn't determine business priority.

items.case: An engineer proposes disabling audit logs to relieve an outage.
items.answer: Choose a targeted supported correction, preserve security logging and include rollback plus functional checks.
items.evidence: Root-cause evidence and follow-up validation criteria.
items.pitfall: Suppressing alerts or logs can hide unresolved security faults.

items.case: Leaders must prioritize two cybersecurity investments.
items.answer: Present verified facts, impact, uncertainty, alternatives, expected risk reduction and decision date.
items.evidence: One-page decision brief tied to technical findings.
items.pitfall: Don't claim modeled risk reduction as a measured certainty.

items.lesson: USB Rubber Ducky: recognition and safe use
items.case: A new unapproved programmable USB peripheral is found.
items.answer: Treat it as untrusted, record physical ownership and evaluate device-control policy through authorized defensive inspection.
items.evidence: Device class, chain of custody and endpoint policy event.
items.pitfall: Appearance alone cannot establish USB behavior.

items.lesson: HackRF One: recognition and safe use
items.case: An SDR is introduced to a beginner wireless lab.
items.answer: Start with permitted receive-only observations, understand frequency restrictions and avoid transmitting without authorization.
items.evidence: Document RF source, applicable rules and observation settings.
items.pitfall: Transmit capability is not permission to radiate.

items.case: An owned demonstration NFC tag is inspected.
items.answer: Identify protocol and separate public identifiers, cryptographic authentication and actual authorization decisions.
items.evidence: Owned media scope, tag capabilities and non-secret observation.
items.pitfall: A card identifier is not the authentication key.

items.lesson: Bash Bunny: recognition and safe use
items.case: A mysterious USB device is handed to an IT analyst.
items.answer: Preserve evidence and inspect only through approved isolated defensive procedures; use endpoint peripheral controls.
items.evidence: Device inventory, policy decision and custody notes.
items.pitfall: Do not execute unknown automation on shared machines.

items.lesson: ESP32 Marauder: recognition and safe use
items.case: Firmware for a wireless development board comes from an unknown mirror.
items.answer: Verify source provenance and approved firmware integrity, then keep tests confined to owned devices under RF rules.
items.evidence: Release version, trusted distribution source and controlled lab notes.
items.pitfall: A successful flash doesn't establish software trustworthiness.

items.lesson: Shark Jack: recognition and safe use
items.case: A portable network testing gadget is offered for office use.
items.answer: Require network owner approval and use a disconnected test switch with owned endpoints for harmless examination.
items.evidence: Isolated topology, consent and tool inventory.
items.pitfall: A physical Ethernet socket is not testing authorization.

items.lesson: O.MG Cable: recognition and safe use
items.case: A cable of uncertain origin is found in the device drawer.
items.answer: Use known-safe accessories, avoid unknown data connections and apply endpoint USB policy.
items.evidence: Asset provenance and defensive peripheral decision.
items.pitfall: A charging-cable appearance doesn't prove data isolation.

items.lesson: Alfa Wi-Fi Adapter: recognition and safe use
items.case: A lab adapter can receive nearby wireless traffic.
items.answer: Operate only on an owned or explicitly approved network with minimal collection and privacy safeguards.
items.evidence: Ownership, monitored channel and data-retention plan.
items.pitfall: Radio reception capability is not blanket permission to capture others' data.

items.lesson: Hardware lab rules and safe boundaries
items.case: A classroom wants to experiment in a shared building network.
items.answer: Document consent, isolated devices, teardown, emergency stop, radio and electrical safety.
items.pitfall: A shared space is not inherently a test environment.

items.lesson: Radio frequency, power and legal compliance
items.case: A transmitter offers user-selectable output power.
items.answer: Confirm frequency allocation, licensing, power and interference requirements before any transmission; favor receive-only practice.
items.evidence: Equipment parameters and regulatory safety checklist.
items.pitfall: Configurable RF hardware doesn't exempt anyone from local rules.

items.case: Two contactless tags provide similar visible identifiers.
items.answer: Differentiate UID, stored data and cryptographic challenge-response; evaluate access policy without cloning credentials.
items.evidence: Owned training-tag protocol notes and authentication concept diagram.
items.pitfall: A visible UID is not proof of authorized access.

items.case: A portable appliance diagram accidentally bridges to the office uplink.
items.answer: Redesign using a disconnected training switch and known endpoints; validate isolation before practice.
items.evidence: Labeled cable paths, power and interface ownership.
items.pitfall: Unintentional bridging can expose unintended networks.

items.case: A low-voltage digital signal shows unexpected pulse length.
items.answer: Verify safe reference ground and supported voltage, select suitable sample rate and compare observed pulse duration with specification.
items.pitfall: Connecting to unknown voltage can damage equipment.

items.case: A board behaves differently after a firmware upgrade.
items.answer: Verify vendor release notes and trusted signatures or checksums where available, document version and safe rollback.
items.evidence: Provenance, before/after behavior and recovery plan.
items.pitfall: A hash obtained from the same compromised source isn't independent assurance.

items.case: An approved test instrument changes custodians.
items.answer: Record serial identifier, responsible person, approved purpose, timestamps, storage and data-handling state.
items.pitfall: Avoid retaining real credentials or unrelated private captures.
